issue_context.title: Scrape imports scan_interval timedelta which leads to JSON serialize errors
issue_context.body:
### The problem

2022.7 beta0 throws errors on migrated scrape sensors. Funny enough, the sensor do seem to get setup correctly.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.7.0b0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Scrape

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/scrape/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
# Yaml config that was imported:

- platform: scrape
  resource: !secret scrape_url_u
  name: "Diesel"
  select: ".field--name-field-station-prices .taxonomy-term-Diesel .field--name-field-prices-price-pump"
  value_template: "{{ value | replace('€', '') | replace('EUR/L', '') | float | round(3) }}"
  unit_of_measurement: €
  scan_interval: 3600

- platform: scrape
  resource: !secret scrape_url_u
  name: "Benzine"
  select: ".field--name-field-station-prices .taxonomy-term-Euro95 .field--name-field-prices-price-pump"
  value_template: "{{ value | replace('€', '') | replace('EUR/L', '') | float | round(3) }}"

```

Hey there @fabaff, @gjohansson-st, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`scrape`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L894) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Something is trying to save a timedelta in a config entry

That's not serializable with `json` either so I think this isn't related to the `json` change, but something is storing a timedelta in the config entry options/data

```python3
import json
import datetime
td = datetime.timedelta(seconds=1)
json.dumps(td)
```
```
% python3 timedelta.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/bdraco/timedelta.py", line 5, in <module>
    json.dumps(td)
  File "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.9/3.9.13_1/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/json/__init__.py", line 231, in dumps
    return _default_encoder.encode(obj)
  File "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.9/3.9.13_1/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/json/encoder.py", line 199, in encode
```

> 2022.7 beta0 throws errors on migrated scrape sensors. Funny enough, the sensor do seem to get setup correctly.

I don't think this is related to scrape.  It just happens to be logged around the same time
@hmmbob 

If I had to guess it looks like some integration added support for changing the scan interval via an options flow and forgot to convert the timedelta to seconds before saving it in the config entry options

$.data.entries[33] and 34 do not exist in .storage/core.config_entries The only thing adding something at this time, and more specifically a timedelta, is the scrape integration, now that is migrated to UI (see `scan_interval`).

The migrated scrape sensors do not appear in config_entries, really making me believe it is these two that trigger the error.

I don't see a scan_interval in the schema for scrape

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f5c6a6be3a0c085c016c3be31985f6bbfd185fc8/homeassistant/components/scrape/config_flow.py#L60

I think its coming in via the import

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f5c6a6be3a0c085c016c3be31985f6bbfd185fc8/homeassistant/components/scrape/sensor.py#L93
So either we should import/convert nicely, or reject this field in the import?
We should remove it from the import
Confirmed fixed in b1, both scrape sensors now also show in core.config_entries

I have a few scrape sensors with custom scan intervals defined in yaml that will be imported when 2022.7 is released next week. Just so I understand the implication with the confirmed fix here, I'll need to disable polling on these entities and use an automation with the homeassistant.update_entity service from then?  Or will scan_interval still be a possible option in the UI?

In case it helps, and to get an idea of my use case, I have some sensors that I only want to update hourly or less (to tease out some data from an external website that updates quite irregularly but not more than a couple times a week at most) and some that I want to update often (say less than every 20-30 seconds), these are artist/album info from radio websites that don't provide great metadata in the audio stream.

I'd be quite fine with the "disable polling + automation rules" route, if that's the correct path.  Just want to prepare for the change(I apologize but I'm not able to run beta for a number of reasons; time, hardware availability and spousal acceptance factors all included).
Correct, disable polling + automation rules is the way to go.
The default can be overridden by defining a `SCAN_INTERVAL` in the sensor platform. We should do that and set it to 5 minutes.

review_comments: nevermind, that's a generic platform config option and not part of the integration.
